question: Consider the function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ given by $f(n)=n^2$. Verify that $f$ is one-one.
explanation:
Equality of images
Let $n_1,n_2\in\mathbb{N}$ and suppose $f(n_1)=f(n_2)$. Then
$$n_1^2=n_2^2.$$

Factorisation
$$n_1^2-n_2^2=0$$
gives
$$(n_1-n_2)(n_1+n_2)=0.$$
Since $n_1,n_2\in\mathbb{N}$, equality of their squares implies
$$n_1=n_2.$$

Conclusion
Hence, $f(n_1)=f(n_2)$ implies $n_1=n_2$, so $f$ is one-one.

options.B: $f$ is not one-one because some natural numbers are not perfect squares
options.D: $f$ is one-one only when the domain contains exactly one natural number
